summary.short: 21 CFR § 870.1345 classifies intravascular bleed monitors, which use bioimpedance and an algorithm to detect internal bleeding, as Class II devices subject to special controls. The controls require specified performance, software, biocompatibility, sterility, shelf-life and labeling data. The text states no effective date.
summary.long: Section 870.1345 of Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations defines an intravascular bleed monitor as a probe, catheter or catheter introducer that measures changes in bioimpedance and uses an algorithm to detect or monitor progression of potential internal bleeding complications. Paragraph (b) classifies the device as Class II (special controls) and lists the special controls. These require in vivo animal performance testing, non-clinical testing of eleven listed characteristics (including tensile, leakage, insertion force and corrosion testing), data supporting sterility, pyrogenicity and shelf life, biocompatibility of patient-contacting components, software verification, validation and hazard analysis, and EMC, electrical, thermal and mechanical safety data. A human factors evaluation must show correct use from the directions for use alone. Labeling must include instructions for use, shelf life and storage conditions, compatible procedures, a sizing table and quantification of blood detected. The text sets out no penalties, enforcement measures or effective date, and does not use the term artificial intelligence.

obligations.summary: Manufacturers of the intravascular bleed monitor must perform in vivo animal performance testing (including gross necropsy and histopathology), non-clinical performance testing of listed characteristics, sterility and pyrogenicity and shelf-life performance data, biocompatibility of patient-contacting components, software verification, validation and hazard analysis, EMC, electrical, thermal and mechanical safety testing, and human factors evaluation.

evidence.quote: In vivo animal performance testing must demonstrate that the device performs as intended under anticipated conditions of use

obligations.summary: Labeling of the device must include instructions for use, a shelf life and storage conditions, compatible procedures, a sizing table, and quantification of blood detected.
